channel.title: JFrog — recent CVEs
channel.description: Most recent CVEs assigned by JFrog (jfrog).

item.title: CVE-2026-82329 · 9.8 CRITICAL 🌩️ — Potential authentication bypass leading to administrative access in Artifactory
item.description: JFrog Artifactory contains an authentication weakness that, under default configuration, may allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to obtain administrative privileges.

item.title: CVE-2026-70550 · 6.5 MEDIUM — Potential unauthorized access to private Composer repository metadata in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: An authorization weakness in JFrog Artifactory Composer repository handling may allow an authenticated user, under specific conditions, to read package metadata from repositories they are not authorized to read. The issue affects confidentiality and…

item.title: CVE-2026-70548 · 3.5 LOW — SSRF In CocoaPods Via JFrog Artifactory External Dependency
item.description: Under specific circumstances, low-level user can run request to remote CocoaPods repos via JFrog Artifactory External Dependency.

item.title: CVE-2026-69104 · 7.6 HIGH — Potential unauthorized repository migration in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: An authenticated user may initiate repository migration operations without required repository permissions, potentially causing information disclosure, unauthorized state changes, and service disruption. Fixed versions address the issue.

item.title: CVE-2026-70551 · 8.5 HIGH — Server-Side Request Forgery Via VCS remote download in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: A user who can read an existing remote VCS repository can replace its configured origin or supply an absolute VCS data URL.

item.title: CVE-2026-69106 · 8.8 HIGH — Potential cache poisoning in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: A low-privileged user may poison cached artifact metadata under specific conditions, potentially causing consumers to retrieve untrusted content.

item.title: CVE-2026-42018 · 7.5 HIGH 🌩️ — Anonymous user token generation exposure in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: JFrog Artifactory could return an internal anonymous-user token to an unauthenticated caller when anonymous access is disabled, potentially exposing sensitive resources.

item.title: CVE-2026-69107 · 5.9 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Potential unauthorized artifact access in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: An unauthenticated user may access restricted artifacts in JFrog Artifactory under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-69105 · 8.1 HIGH 🌩️ — Potential package cache integrity issue in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: An unauthenticated attacker may cause untrusted package content to be cached under specific conditions, potentially affecting artifact integrity and availability.

item.title: CVE-2026-70547 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Potential unauthorized metadata exposure in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: An authenticated user without repository read permission may access package metadata under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-66016 · 6.7 MEDIUM — Rendered Artifactory Helm manifests may contain generated TLS private keys
item.description: Under specific self-hosted Helm configurations, generated TLS private keys may be retained in rendered manifests accessible to highly privileged local users.

item.title: CVE-2026-68759 · 7.2 HIGH — Integration credential holders may impersonate users in JFrog Access
item.description: A holder of a valid integration credential may impersonate other users under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-65926 · 3.1 LOW — Private Release Bundle versions may be disclosed under specific configurations
item.description: An anonymous caller when anonymous access is enabled, or a low-privilege authenticated user, may learn private Release Bundle names and versions when the bundle name is known.

item.title: CVE-2026-66384 · 5.3 MEDIUM 💥 — Authenticated users may write data outside the intended Docker cache path
item.description: An authenticated user may write data outside the intended Docker cache path under specific remote-repository conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68758 · 6.5 MEDIUM — Authenticated users may access restricted Artifactory support information
item.description: A low-privileged authenticated user may access restricted support information under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-66375 · 8.1 HIGH — Low-privilege users may remove protected Artifactory metadata
item.description: A low-privilege authenticated user may permanently remove protected internal metadata across repositories under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68757 · 7.5 HIGH — Potential improper SAML signature verification in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: A user with access to a valid SAML response may impersonate another user under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68756 · 6.6 MEDIUM — Potential insecure deserialization in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: A party with write access to stored session data may affect JFrog Artifactory under specific conditions.

item.description: An authenticated user may write files outside the intended Artifactory work directory under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-66381 · 5.3 MEDIUM — Repository readers may access content outside configured upstream paths
item.description: A repository reader with cache-deploy permission may access content outside a configured upstream path under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68760 · 5.3 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Potential remember-me authentication bypass in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: An unauthenticated user may bypass authentication under specific cache conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-66379 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Authenticated users may view private Puppet module metadata
item.description: An authenticated user may view private Puppet module metadata without repository read access.

item.title: CVE-2026-66378 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Authenticated users may access private NuGet metadata
item.description: An authenticated user without repository read permission may access private NuGet metadata under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-66377 · 5.3 MEDIUM 🌩️ — Anonymous users may access restricted Artifactory repository information
item.description: An unauthenticated user may access restricted repository information under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68755 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Bundle writers may alter trusted release information in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: A bundle writer may create misleading release promotion information under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-66380 · 4.3 MEDIUM — Authenticated users may access private OCI referrer metadata
item.description: An authenticated user without repository read permission may access private OCI referrer metadata under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68754 · 6.5 MEDIUM — Publishers without delete permission can overwrite docker layer information
item.description: A repository publisher without delete permission may modify protected package content under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68753 · 5.3 MEDIUM — Anonymous users may access restricted Artifactory content under specific configurations
item.description: An unauthenticated user may access restricted Artifactory content when a credentialed remote repository is configured in a specific way.

item.title: CVE-2026-66376 · 4.2 MEDIUM — Deleted users may temporarily retain access to JFrog Artifactory
item.description: Credentials for a deleted user may remain valid for a short period under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-68752 · 7.2 HIGH — Project Resource Managers may escalate privileges in JFrog Artifactory
item.description: A Project Resource Manager may gain broader administrative privileges under specific conditions.

item.description: An authorization weakness in JFrog Artifactory internal metadata handling could allow a user with limited repository access to write to restricted internal metadata areas under specific conditions. Successful abuse is limited to integrity and availab…

item.title: CVE-2026-65923 · 6.8 MEDIUM — Potential server-side request forgery in Artifactory Ansible repository handling
item.description: A URL validation weakness in JFrog Artifactory Ansible repository handling could allow a user, under specific repository access conditions, to cause unintended server-side requests. The issue primarily affects confidentiality and integrity and has be…

item.title: CVE-2026-65617 · 8.8 HIGH — Potential remote code execution on an Artifactory package service container.
item.description: A deserialization weakness in JFrog Artifactory package handling could allow a low-privileged user to impact confidentiality, integrity, and availability under specific repository conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-65924 · 6.5 MEDIUM — Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via Terraform Remote repository
item.description: JFrog Artifactory support for Terraform remote repositories was found to be susceptible to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). An authenticated user - or, if anonymous access is enabled on the repository, an unauthenticated user - could cause Artifac…

item.title: CVE-2026-65925 · 6.5 MEDIUM — Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via JFrog Artifactory Cargo remote repository
item.description: A user with JFrog Artifactory Cargo remote repository read access could make Artifactory request unintended URLs and return the response.

item.title: CVE-2026-65616 · 8.8 HIGH — Potential privilege escalation to JFrog administrator privileges
item.description: Incorrect authorization validation in refresh token signature allows non-admin users to obtain a signed JFrog administrator token.

item.title: CVE-2026-66015 · 7.2 HIGH — JFrog Platform contains an authorization flaw that may allow authenticated privilege escalation.
item.description: An authenticated privilege-escalation vulnerability in JFrog Platform may be exploited under admin-provisioned account conditions. Successful exploitation may grant temporary platform administrator access.

item.title: CVE-2026-65618 · 6.5 MEDIUM — Improper URL validation when handling specific URLs Pub, Terraform and Docker packages might lead to SSRF vulnerability
item.description: Improper URL validation when handling specific URLs, allows an attacker, under certain conditions, to make unauthorized requests from JFrog Artifactory, potentially exposing internal services and cached response data.

item.title: CVE-2026-66018 · 6.5 MEDIUM — JFrog Artifactory build environment properties exposure
item.description: Build readers can access another repository's environment properties. A caller with read access to an ordinary repository can select a readable repository parameter while retrieving environment properties for a protected build, exposing build environ…

item.title: CVE-2026-66014 · 8.8 HIGH — Potential authentication bypass leading to privilege escalation in Artifactory
item.description: JFrog Artifactory contains an authentication handling weakness in internal request processing that, under specific conditions, may allow an attacker to escalate privileges beyond the intended access level.

item.title: CVE-2026-65921 · 8.8 HIGH — Potential path traversal leading to unauthorized file writes
item.description: A path validation weakness in archive extraction/write handling allows entries with traversal sequences to be written outside the intended build artifacts location.

item.title: CVE-2026-42017 · 8.8 HIGH — Privilege escalation via JFrog Worker event token exposure
item.description: An event-handling weakness in JFrog Artifactory could expose privileged authorization material to a lower-privileged user under specific conditions.

item.title: CVE-2026-42016 · 8.1 HIGH — Incorrect authorization validation of user token in JFrog Artifactory allows Privilege Escalation
item.description: JFrog Artifactory (Self Hosted) versions before 7.133.11 are vulnerable to a privilege escalation attack due to a validation check of the token signature/issuer and not the token’s scope.
